newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - May 6.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Constitution Drafting Assembly has sounded a warning against attempts by politicians to hijack the political reform process. Attempts to manipulate and undermine the fundamentals of the proposals during the scrutiny stage could provoke the resignation of many key figures in the drive. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Defence Ministry has signed a memorandum of understanding allowing the United States to use Thailand's satellite orbital slots in exchange for the use of six transponders on a U.S. satellite. Under the plan, the military will spend only 15 billion baht for leasing capacity and the purchase of ground station facilities, much less than the 28 billion baht the Defence Minstry initially planned to spend on two military satellites under the so-called Star of Siam project. (THE NATION)

- More than 100 passengers have filed complaints with police seeking compensation from Songserm Service Co, operator of the ferry that sank near Koh Phi Phi on Sunday. The group, mostly school teachers from Nakhon Pathom province, was among 600 Thai and foreign tourists picked up from the sea by naval rescuers after the King Cruise hit a coral reef and took in water. (BANGKOK POST)

- Thai Petrochemical Industry (TPI) will fuel its petrochemical project with an additional investment of 10 billion baht if the government ends the gas distribution monopoly held by the Petroleum Authority of Thailand. TPI has contacted Unocal Thailand, a developer of gas fields in the Gulf of Thailand, and has been promised delivery of 180 million cubic feet per day. (BUSINESS DAY)

- Thai rice exporters have suffered combined losses of more than two billion baht last year due to forward contracts with under-estimated prices. Meanwhile the Rice Exporters Association has reported rice export volume in the first three months fell 30 percent over the same period last year to 1.04 million tonnes because of higher prices than those of competitor countries as well as limited supplies. (THE NATION)
